content.title: About
content.content: Whole grain fruit waffles are a ready‑to‑eat frozen product made from whole‑grain flour, berries or fruit pieces, and a modest amount of sugar. They feature a crisp golden exterior and a soft, aromatic interior, retaining much of the fiber and vitamins thanks to the whole grain and fruit components.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Whole‑grain waffles contain more dietary fiber than traditional white‑flour waffles.
Fruits such as blueberry, strawberry or apple retain a portion of their antioxidants even after freezing.
The waffles can be stored in the freezer and cooked quickly in a toaster or microwave.
In several countries they are marketed as a "grab‑and‑go" breakfast and are popular among athletes.
Flash‑freezing technology preserves texture and flavor without the need for added preservatives.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Whole‑grain flour provides dietary fiber that supports healthy digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Whole grains contain thiamine, niacin and folate, essential for energy metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidants from fruit
items.content: Berries and fruit add vitamin C and polyphenols that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Lower glycemic impact
items.content: The combination of whole grain and fruit leads to a slower rise in blood sugar compared with regular waffles.

items.title: Quick energy source
items.content: Carbohydrates from the grain and fruit are readily available, making the waffles convenient before workouts or as a snack.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: The product contains wheat, so individuals with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity should choose a gluten‑free alternative.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: While moderate, the sugar should be accounted for by those monitoring blood glucose levels.

items.title: Risk of under‑heating
items.content: If not heated properly, the waffles may remain cold inside, increasing the risk of food‑borne illness.

items.title: Preservatives in long‑term storage
items.content: Some brands add small amounts of preservatives to extend shelf life; check the label if you are sensitive.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Toast the frozen waffles for 2–3 minutes until golden and crisp. Serve with yogurt, honey, nut butter, or fresh berries to enhance flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the waffles in a sealed bag in the freezer at –18 °C. After thawing, consume within 24 hours and do not leave at room temperature for more than 2 hours.
